title: Documenta / Graecorum Concilia
author: Incertus
source: Translated by Claude from tmp1450.tmp1450.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

passages.original: Haec esi fides quam exposuerunt Patres : primum quidem adversus Arium blasphemum dicentem crea- turam esse Filium Dei : et adversus omnem haeresem Sabellii, Photini, Pauli Samosateni, Manichaei, Va- lentini, Marcionis, et adversus omnem omnino haere- sem, si qua insurrexerit contra catholicam et aposto- licam Ecclesiam : quas omnes condemnarunt Nicaeam congregati episcopi trecenti decem et octo quorum nomina et provinciae conscriptae sunt : sed plerique studiosi servi Dei magis curam gesserunt Orientalium episcoporum nomina describere, propter hoc quod Occidens non similiter inquisitionem de haeresibus habuerit o.
passages.english: This is the faith which the Fathers set forth: first of all against Arius the blasphemer, who said that the Son of God is a creature; and against every heresy of Sabellius, Photinus, Paul of Samosata, Mani, Valentinus, Marcion; and against absolutely every heresy, if any should rise up against the catholic and apostolic Church. All these [heresies] the three hundred and eighteen bishops gathered at Nicaea condemned, whose names and provinces have been written down; but most of the zealous servants of God took greater care to record the names of the Eastern bishops, because the West did not have a similar inquiry concerning heresies.
passages.notes: "esi" read as "est" (scanning error). The final "o" after "habuerit" appears to be a stray footnote mark and has been omitted. "Manichaei" is rendered as Mani, the founder of the Manichaeans.

passages.original: Quicunque ergo vel in hac sacra urbe, vel in Alexandrina civitate, vel in omni Aegyptiaca dioecese diversisque aliis provinciis Euty- chetis profanam perversitatem sequuntur, et ita non credunt ut trecenti decem et octo sancti Patres tra- diderunt catholicam fidem in Nicaea civitate fun- dantes, centum quoque et quinquaginta alii venera- biles episcopi qui in hac alma urbe Constantinopo- litana postea convenerunt, sicut Athanasius et Theo- philus et Cyrillus sanctae recordationis episcopi Alexandrinae civitatis credebant, quos [T. 1, 2, quod] etiam Ephesitana synodus cui beatae memoriae Cyrillus praefuit, in qua Nestorii error expulsus est, in universis secuta est, quos et nuper venerabilis Chalcedone synodus est secula, prioribus conciliis sacerdotum ex omni prorsus parte consentientibus, nihilque adimens a sacrosancto symbolo neque ad- jiciens, sed Eutychetis dogmata funesta condem- nans;
passages.english: Whoever, therefore, whether in this sacred city, or in the city of Alexandria, or in the whole Egyptian diocese and various other provinces, follow the profane perversity of Eutyches, and do not believe as the three hundred and eighteen holy Fathers handed down when they founded the catholic faith in the city of Nicaea, and also the hundred and fifty other venerable bishops who afterwards assembled in this kindly city of Constantinople, [and] as Athanasius and Theophilus and Cyril, bishops of holy remembrance of the city of Alexandria, believed, whom the synod of Ephesus also, over which Cyril of blessed memory presided and in which the error of Nestorius was expelled, followed in all things, and whom the venerable synod of Chalcedon has also recently followed, agreeing in absolutely every respect with the earlier councils of bishops, and neither taking anything away from the most sacred creed nor adding [anything], but condemning the deadly doctrines of Eutyches;
passages.notes: The edition records a variant 'quod' for 'quos' ("which" for "whom"). 'secula' is read as 'secuta' (followed).
